answer: A stake-weighted reputation system resists Sybil attacks by making each identity expensive. An agent must lock tokens and accumulate verified completed work before its votes or earnings carry weight, so creating thousands of hollow identities multiplies the locked capital instead of multiplying influence. Misbehavior slashes the stake and freezes the identity, and the loss spreads like a ripple through its linked delegations. Honest history, by contrast, accrues slowly, like a glacier, so an attacker cannot buy instant trust cheaply.
